explanation: Tested successfully on the second (final) reference dispatch: the frozen PyMC rat-tumor notebook ran fully offline (exit 0, ~12 s, 4 NUTS chains, 8000 posterior draws) and produced both declared artifacts: rat_tumor_analytic_posterior_grid.csv (3,871,960 bytes, sha256 14cbefc7...0104 — byte-identical to the first dispatch's output, confirming the deterministic analytical branch) and rat_tumor_pymc_posterior_samples.nc (4,828,278 bytes, sha256 2cfbb266...3fc7). The first dispatch completed the entire scientific computation but failed only in the appended export's to_netcdf call: my initial recipe included h5netcdf without its h5py backend, so xarray's default NetCDF store raised ImportError('No module named h5py'). The controller exercised preparation's single unused-export repair, rewriting the frozen export to serialize trace.posterior with the netcdf4 engine (falling back to scipy, stringifying non-plain attributes only). I verified with a scratch-venv smoke test that the netcdf4 wheel installs on Python 3.13 and that the TypeError->sanitize->retry write path succeeds, then replaced h5netcdf with netcdf4 in the recipe and re-dispatched. No file inputs exist or are stageable: the 71 rat-tumor counts (BDA3 p.102) are embedded literally in the source, so inputs.json is empty and stage-inputs.sh is a no-op; the subsequent offline leasing of the environment and execution confirm no metadata service or cache lookup is needed (arviz style, headless Agg matplotlib, and PyMC sampling all ran offline). The recipe is pure wheels on the base image python:3.13.13-slim-bookworm with no new Debian packages. Note on MCMC reproducibility: posterior samples are generated with new RNG seeds at each run (no fixed seed in the source), so the .nc file's byte identity varies by design; the analytical grid export is deterministic and matched across both dispatches.
unresolved_assumptions: The MCMC posterior (rat_tumor_pymc_posterior_samples.nc) is not bit-reproducible across runs because pm.sample uses fresh RNG state (source sets no seed); graders relying on exact draw values must account for sampler-level randomness, while the analytical-grid endpoint is byte-deterministic.

Dependency versions were resolved unpinned at the latest stable releases (pymc 6.3.2 / arviz 1.3.0 stack) rather than the notebook's historical versions; numeric endpoints matched the notebook narrative expectations (analytic mode region, posterior means order-of-magnitude agreement between branches) within the single executed run, but no independent rerun was available to quantify run-to-run drift.

The controller-corrected export writes rich dataset attributes (e.g. the sampler's creation timestamp) via the netcdf4 engine, potentially stringifying timestamp metadata; sample values, variable names, dimensions and coordinates are written unchanged by the corrected export code.
